llm.summary: The package is internally consistent with its stated purpose — it contains LMail ops scripts that require a base URL and local credentials and do not surreptitiously exfiltrate data — but you should still review who you run it with and which base_url you point it at before executing admin actions.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (LMail operations: registration, auth, inbox, admin) align with the code and runtime requirements. Declared binaries (python3, curl) and required config (lmail.base_url / LMAIL_BASE_URL) are appropriate for HTTP-based ops against an LMail service. No unrelated cloud credentials or unrelated binaries are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run included scripts (registration, PoW solve, inbox polling, admin audit/override). Those scripts legitimately perform network calls to the configured base_url, read and write a local credentials file (default .lmail-credentials.json), and can persist API keys/tokens. This is expected for an ops skill, but it means secrets will be stored locally and networked to the given base_url. SKILL.md and scripts use an example domain (https://amiigzz.online) — treat that as an example only and do not point credentials or run admin flows against that domain unless you trust it.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No package-level install specification downloads arbitrary code. The skill is distributed with all scripts included (no network install steps). The included install helper (install_for_openclaw.sh) can copy the skill into a target directory if you run it, but there are no remote downloads or archive extractions in the package.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests minimal environment/config (lmail.base_url and optional LMAIL_CREDENTIALS_FILE). Scripts accept admin-token or admin-api-key arguments and will fall back to the credentials file. That is proportionate to admin/ops functionality, but those admin credentials are sensitive — the scripts will use them to call admin endpoints (e.g., override-permit) and may persist returned apiKey/token to the credentials file (save_json_file sets file mode to 0600 when possible). Review and control which credentials you supply.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and model invocation allowed (default) — appropriate for an invocable skill. The package will not auto-install itself unless you explicitly run install_for_openclaw.sh or publish_clawhub.sh. Running those helper scripts can write into skill directories or create a temporary git snapshot; these are explicit actions and not automatic.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says: a collection of scripts to operate an LMail service. Key precautions before using it: 1) Do not point LMAIL_BASE_URL to an untrusted external host — the scripts will send credentials and messages to whatever base_url you provide; the example domain (amiigzz.online) in docs is only illustrative and should not be used unless you trust it. 2) Treat admin-token / admin-api-key as highly sensitive: only provide them when you intend to perform admin flows (e.g., override-permit) and preferably from a controlled environment. 3) The scripts persist credentials to a local file (default .lmail-credentials.json); ensure it's stored in a secure location and audited. 4) Review the included scripts (they are plain Python/Bash) before running, especially ones that perform admin actions or publishing (publish_clawhub.sh, install_for_openclaw.sh). 5) Run dangerous actions (admin overrides, publish) in a sandbox or with a disposable account if you are uncertain. If you want higher assurance, ask the author for: (a) the intended production base_url, (b) justification for any admin flows you plan to run, and (c) a short security review or signed release provenance for the package.
